title: 💻 Claude Code Best Practices 2026: Anthropic's Official Advice
content:
Claude Code 技术干货

Summary: The Claude Code best practices Anthropic recommends in November 2026 come down to three moves: tell Claude what it cannot see in your code, give it a check it can run that returns pass or fail, and enforce the few rules that can never be broken with hooks, deny rules or managed settings instead of prompts. Keep CLAUDE.md short (Anthropic's memory guide suggests under 200 lines), use /clear between unrelated tasks, and put a person in charge of approving anything you cannot undo. [...] Before Claude Code runs unattended, make sure it knows what done looks like, can check its own work, can only touch what it should, has a cap on turns or spend, and hands its result to a person for sign-off. Anthropic frames these as five questions to ask about each specific task.

Unattended runs still end with a person approving the merge or deploy. Photo: Getty Images / Unsplash+ [...] Most "Claude Code best practices" lists still repeat 2025-era advice: shout IMPORTANT in your instructions, type "think harder," and guard the context window at all costs. Anthropic's own Claude Code best practices page now says several of those habits are no longer needed, because current models follow plain instructions and run with a 1M-token window on most models.

title: 💻 Claude Code Best Practices: Anthropic's Checklist | Xtrusio
content:
Claude Code 技术干货

### Before you let Claude run on its own

Make sure Claude knows what done looks like and can check its work. Limit what it can touch. Set a cap on turns or spend, then have a person approve the result.

Tell Claude what it cannot see, give it a check to run, enforce the hard rules, and steer the session.

## Advice you can stop following

Anthropic's current guide drops two habits that older guides still repeat. [...] ## Short answer

Use Claude Code well by giving it context, a pass-or-fail check and a few enforced rules. Put only facts it cannot see in `CLAUDE.md`. Give it a test, build or lint command and ask for the output. Use a hook, deny rule or managed setting when a rule cannot have exceptions. A hook runs an action automatically, a deny rule blocks listed actions, and a managed setting locks an organization policy. [...] | Question | Claude weighs it (guideline) | Claude Code enforces it (every time) |
 --- 
| What should it do? | Prompt, `CLAUDE.md` or skill | Hook when the action must happen |
| What can it touch? | A plain-language boundary | Deny rule or managed setting |
| When is it done? | Definition of done in the prompt | Stop hook that runs the check |

Source: Anthropic, Claude Code best practices, read 3 November 2026.

Choose `/batch` when applying bulk changes across an entire project. Choose headless mode when embedding AI processing into existing CI/CD pipelines.

## /batch Command: Parallel Execution of Large-Scale Code Changes

### Basic Usage

`/batch` is a bundled skill invoked with slash-command syntax inside an interactive Claude Code session.1 It researches the repository, proposes 5–30 independent units, waits for plan approval, and then creates one worktree-isolated background agent per unit.2 [...] SmartScope · Generative AI

# Claude Code /batch vs claude -p: Parallel Changes or CI Automation

Choose Claude Code /batch for 5–30 worktree-isolated agents and pull requests, or claude -p for scripts and CI. Includes current limits and safe use cases.

Claude Code has two different ways to run work at scale. Use `/batch` to split one repository-wide change across independent worktrees and pull requests. Use `claude -p` when a script or CI job needs one non-interactive result. [...] This article reflects information as of JST. The information may have been updated since then; check the official source for the latest.

## Key Points

Key Points

- `/batch` is a bundled skill that plans 5–30 independent units and runs each in an isolated Git worktree
- Headless mode (`claude -p`) provides non-interactive integration for CI/CD pipelines and shell scripts
- The two serve distinctly different use cases and can be combined to automate the entire development workflow

content:
Claude Code 技术干货

Claude Code tackles this with two commands worth knowing: `/simplify` and `/batch`. The `/simplify` command analyzes code and surfaces concrete ways to reduce complexity without changing behavior. The `/batch` command lets you run operations across multiple files simultaneously, so large refactors don’t require running the same prompt over and over.

Here’s how both work and when to use them.

## What Claude Code Is [...] When you invoke `/batch`, Claude Code breaks your task into discrete units — one per file, or one per defined scope — and runs them concurrently using multiple Claude instances. Each subagent operates independently on its assigned scope. [...] `/batch` is designed for situations where you need to apply the same operation across many files or make multiple related changes simultaneously. Instead of running the same prompt file by file, you describe what you want done, tell Claude Code which files to target, and it handles execution in parallel.

content:
Claude Code 技术干货

## Why `/batchy`?

The skill was originally named `/batch`, but Claude Code introduced a built-in `/batch` command with different semantics (#4). To avoid the collision, we renamed to `/batchy`. Existing installs are migrated automatically when you re-run `./install.sh`.

## Usage

### Submit work to batch

In Claude Code, just say:

```
/batchy Review this codebase for security issues 
```

```
/batchy Generate comprehensive tests for src/auth/ 
``` [...] MCP Server (`claude_batch_mcp.py`): Python script run by `uv`. Exposes `send_to_batch`, `batch_status`, `batch_fetch`, `batch_list`, `batch_poll_once` tools. Also works as a CLI.
 Skill (`SKILL.md`): Teaches Claude Code how and when to use the batch tools. Invoked with `/batchy`. Loaded automatically.
 Status Line (`statusline.sh`): Bash script that renders batch job counts in the Claude Code status bar and triggers background polling via `curl`+`jq`. [...] ```
/batchy Write API documentation for all public endpoints 
```

Claude will gather all relevant context, build a self-contained prompt, submit it to the Batch API, and tell you the job ID.

### Check results

```
/batchy check 
```

```
/batchy status 
```

```
/batchy list 
```

Results appear in your status bar automatically. When a job completes, Claude reads the result from disk and presents it.
